plain: To conquer and bring under control

webster.text: To subdue and bring under the yoke of power or dominion; to conquer by force and compel to submit to the government or absolute control of another.

example.quote: Gentlemen had suggested that the seat of government would become a sanctuary for state villains, and that, in a short time, ten miles square would subjugate a country of eight hundred miles square.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 16, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
